name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Implement a shadow test on the new prompt before a full rollout. This allows us to observe how the changes perform in a controlled setting with real users, enabling us to catch hidden issues that could degrade quality. The trade-off is the delay in wider deployment, but this minimizes risk and ensures a smoother transition, aligning with the goal of prioritizing quality.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow testing only catches failures users notice—it misses silent quality drops like a prompt that subtly biases answers toward shorter, less accurate responses. A better alternative is canary deployments with automated quality gates that compare answer accuracy, not just user complaints. Settle it by running both: shadow test for user-visible issues, canary with strict quality metrics for hidden degradation.
